body:
verify-all.sh failed on this machine (2026-07-16):
`SettingsScreenTest > initials load from the server and can be edited and saved
(T-64)` — ComparisonFailure expected:<[XY]> but was:<[MI]> at line 193
(server pytest and web vitest/tsc/lint both green; the other 250 Android tests
pass).

Root cause is a wait-for-the-wrong-thing race, same family as T-66: the test
clicks Save, then `composeTestRule.waitForIdle()`, then asserts
`viewModel.uiState.value.initials == "XY"`. waitForIdle() only waits for
Compose to go idle — updateInitials() runs a real MockWebServer round trip on
OkHttp's dispatcher, which Compose knows nothing about. On a fast machine the
response usually lands first; on slow hardware it loses the race and the
assertion still sees the GET-loaded "MI".

Fix: await the actual condition, not idleness — e.g.
`composeTestRule.waitUntil(timeoutMillis) { viewModel.uiState.value.initials == "XY" }`
before the assert (and sweep SettingsScreenTest's sibling tests for the same
click-then-waitForIdle-then-assert-network-result pattern).
title: Android: SettingsScreenTest initials-save test is flaky — waitForIdle races the MockWebServer round trip
